summary: The note is a first-person feature on efforts since September 2023 to restore and protect the Greenwood Wetlands. It covers advocate Anna Perkins, the Greenwood Initiative led by Dr. Hector Gonzalez, youth education tours, the Rewilding Greenwood project, drone mapping, volunteers, a corporate-government partnership, and pending wetland protection legislation.
one_line: A feature on community, educational, technological, corporate and legislative efforts to restore the Greenwood Wetlands since September 2023.
key_facts: The author first visited the Greenwood Wetlands in October 2023 and met Anna Perkins, a retired school teacher turned wetland advocate.
Anna Perkins recalled that as a child the wetlands were brimming with life, with herons and dragonflies, before they began to disappear.
The Greenwood Initiative is spearheaded by local environmentalist Dr. Hector Gonzalez, who began community meetings in late 2023.
Dr. Hector Gonzalez said at a February 15, 2024 community meeting that protecting the wetlands is 'a commitment that traverses various disciplines and backgrounds'.
Naturalist Sarah Li launched the 'Wonders of the Wetlands' tour on November 2, 2023, which has connected over a thousand children to the wetlands.
'Rewilding Greenwood' was rolled out on May 5, 2024, reintroducing native plants and removing invasive species.
Ecologist Emily Zhang pioneered drone imaging to create detailed habitat maps, implemented on December 3, 2023.
Emily Zhang described drones as 'an eye in the sky' that sees what people often can't.
Carpenter Joe Baxter, met planting saplings in January 2024, volunteers at the wetlands and said 'we're planting hope'.
On September 17, 2023, the Magnolia Corporation teamed up with the local government to fund the 'Greenwood Revival Project'.
Assemblyman Mark Richards has championed bills for stronger wetland protection, with one crucial policy up for vote in late 2024.
